body:
Good morning, Kern County. We’re waking up to a clear, warm Tuesday, and today’s top story comes with a heavy heart: a pedestrian was killed over the weekend during a police pursuit in Oildale, and the community is demanding answers. It’s a mild start at 70 degrees at Meadows Field, with air quality in the moderate range, so it’s a good day to keep windows open and step outside before the heat builds.

## The Kern Overnight

Fire crews had a busy night across the county, starting with a structure fire that broke out near Mount Vernon Avenue and Niles Street on the east side of Bakersfield just before 1 a.m. A passerby spotted smoke coming from a building, and the call brought a heavy response — multiple engines, two trucks and battalion chiefs. Crews knocked the fire down within about 15 minutes, completed a primary search and stayed on scene for roughly half an hour before clearing. No injuries were reported.

Just before dawn, a vehicle fire sparked in a hotel parking lot on Marriott Drive. A caller reported that a car had struck a parked vehicle, which then caught fire, and a second caller feared someone might still be inside the burning car. Fire crews and an ambulance were sent to the scene as a precaution.

On the other side of town, a grass fire in the Hageman Road area smoldered with light smoke overnight. Crews said it was contained to an irrigation area with no immediate threat to structures. Firefighters made contact with the landowner and planned to return this morning with heavy equipment to make sure it was fully out.

Deputies also handled two possible domestic incidents overnight. The first was reported in the Paramount Colony area late Monday, where a caller said the driver of a dark sedan holding a toddler had left an In-N-Out parking lot while a domestic disturbance was in progress. The vehicle’s direction remained unknown, and deputies responded to the area. The second was called in before dawn at an apartment complex on White Lane, after a neighbor heard a woman screaming and a man shouting. Dispatchers kept an open line with a woman who was crying and treated the call as a possible domestic incident in progress.

Elsewhere in the log: a caller flagged officers down near 2nd Street after an apparent assault, and medical aid was staged for the victim at the scene. Officers and medics also responded to a home on Brown Street for a man reported to have blood on his clothing and to be off his medications. Deputies were asked to check on a man and a woman reported sleeping in the canal area along Gosford Road, and a stranded motorist on Interstate 5 north of Quebec said she had been broken down on the shoulder since the previous day.

## Today's weather

Expect a hot one: high near 96 degrees today, with a low around 73 tonight. It’s currently a pleasant 70 degrees at Meadows Field. No weather alerts are active for Kern County, so conditions should stay calm and dry. Air quality checks in at 54, which is moderate — sensitive groups might want to take it easy outdoors during the peak of the afternoon heat. No active fires are burning locally.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a pedestrian was killed during a police pursuit in Oildale early Saturday morning, and the community is demanding answers.** Bakersfield Police were chasing a suspect wanted on firearm possession and gang charges when police say a driver picked the suspect up and sped away down Airport Drive south of Olive. Officers deployed spike strips; the vehicle spun out and slammed into a pedestrian, who died at the scene. Police have not yet identified the male victim, and community members have placed flowers where he fell. Two men were arrested: 21-year-old Isaiah Andrade and 20-year-old Gabriel Lopez. Lopez, the driver, faces a second-degree murder charge and is being held on bail of more than $1 million. BPD says both suspects have prior charges. Oildale resident Buddy Stone told the station the incident has left neighbors scared to walk the streets, asking, "Am I gonna be the one today?"

**KGET 17 reports on the growing controversy around that same deadly crash, with questions mounting about the decision to pursue.** The station notes the pursuit happened on a Saturday, and the loss of life has put a spotlight on Bakersfield Police chase policies. Neighbors in Oildale are said to be shaken, with some calling for a closer look at when and how officers chase suspects through residential neighborhoods. KGET also reports the department’s response to the crash is under review.

**Bakersfield Now reports that gun-related homicides are down in Bakersfield, even after a recent high school shooting.** The station cites BPD data showing a downward trend in gun deaths so far this year, despite the high-profile shooting that rattled the community. Officials are said to be crediting a mix of enforcement and community intervention efforts, though they acknowledge the recent school shooting is a reminder that one incident can alter the statistics.

**KGET 17 reports that union power is growing in the Central Valley’s political world after this year’s Labor Day demonstrations.** The station covered the Stramler Park gathering where hundreds of workers and families came together, but the story goes deeper: labor leaders say their organizations are becoming more involved in local and state elections. They argue that working families need a stronger voice in policy decisions, and unions are positioning themselves to be that voice in the valley.

**KGET 17 also reports that Raven Aviation in Kernville has temporarily closed due to a "severe vermin infestation," according to Kern County Public Health.** The closure was ordered after inspectors found the problem at the Kern River Valley business. The owner is working with health officials to resolve the issue before reopening. The temporary closure has grounded operations at the aviation facility, which serves pilots and the local community.

**23ABC reports that Kern County workers gathered at Stramler Park to celebrate Labor Day, honoring the contributions of the workforce while voicing concerns about job security and automation.** Alissa Reed, executive secretary of the Kern, Inyo, and Mono Counties Building and Construction Trades Council, told the station the event is about recognizing the role workers play in society and the economy. Union members attended with their families, including Attila Bachman, who brought his grandson to support local workers. Sandy Reding, a Bakersfield Memorial Hospital operating room nurse and representative with the California Nurses Association, reminded attendees that the eight-hour day, weekends and paid holidays were won through organizing. The holiday carried an edge this year as conversations about artificial intelligence and workplace safety took center stage.

**23ABC reports that the 988 crisis line answered more than 40,000 calls, chats and texts in Kern County over the past year**, setting up today’s 988 Day resource fair and blood drive at Beale Memorial Library. The Kern Behavioral Health and Recovery Services team handled over 7,000 contacts involving current or past suicidal thoughts. Tyler Frost told the station the staff has "saved a lot of lives." Today’s fair runs from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. and will include suicide prevention resources, safety plan training and coping workbooks, plus a blood drive in partnership with Houchin Community Blood Bank.

## Something good

There was real warmth to be found at Stramler Park over the holiday weekend. Hundreds of Kern County workers and their families gathered for the annual Labor Day picnic, a day meant to celebrate the people who keep this valley running — the nurses, the builders, the teachers, the folks who show up every day. Between the food and the festivities, union members brought their grandchildren and their stories, carrying on a tradition that stretches back generations. As Sandy Reding put it, the benefits workers enjoy today weren’t handed out; they were won, and the next generation was there to see it. It’s a reminder that even as technology changes the workplace, the people doing the work deserve to be seen.

## Coming up this week

Today’s big one is the second annual 988 Day Resource Fair and Blood Drive at Beale Memorial Library, happening from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. in partnership with Kern Behavioral Health and Recovery Services and Houchin Community Blood Bank. It’s part of Suicide Prevention Awareness Month and includes suicide prevention resources, safety plan training, coping workbooks and other community resources.

The Fox Theater has a full week of entertainment ahead. Comedian Justin Willman brings his "One For The Ages" tour to town on Thursday, September 10. Max Amini takes the stage for a live show in Bakersfield on Saturday, September 12. Country artist Clay Walker stops by with his "Doin' What I Love Tour" on Sunday, September 13. The Fox’s "Cults & Classics" series rolls on with a screening of the Coen Brothers' "Fargo" on Monday, September 14, and the nostalgia continues with "It's A 2000s Party: Bakersfield" on Friday, September 18.

For those planning the week ahead, library resources are also part of a month-long partnership between Kern Behavioral Health and the Kern County Library, which includes mental health resources and a curated book list at Beale Memorial Library. Suicide prevention isn’t just about knowing the warning signs, as Tyler Frost told 23ABC — it’s about starting conversations and checking in on the people around you.
